background_notes.fact: For periodic A in L2, ||Dinv A||_2<=||A||_2. Also ||h||_2<=||h||_(H^s) for s>=0, in particular s=1 and s=gamma here.

grounds.reason: Sobolev norms are the specified weighted Fourier-square sums.
L2 is H^0 with the normalized spatial norm.
Dinv has multiplier (ik)^(-1) for nonzero integer k and zero at k=0.

background_notes.justification: For each nonzero integer k, |k|^(-2)<=1; summing gives the Dinv contraction. For s>=0 every weight (1+k^2)^s is at least one, giving the Sobolev-to-L2 bounds. These statements are uniform in Fourier support.

background_notes.fact: For a smooth Banach-space-valued function A(t)=integral_a^t G(s)ds, A'=G and ||A(t)||<=integral_a^t||G(s)||ds. A bounded linear spatial multiplier commutes with this integral. Thus, when Y_n(t_n)=0 and sup||Dinv Y_n'||_2<=K, sup_(I_n)||Dinv Y_n||_2<=tau K.

background_notes.justification: For smooth integrands, the fundamental theorem of calculus holds in the L2 Hilbert space, by taking difference quotients of the integral. The triangle inequality for the integral follows from Riemann sums and passage to their norm limit. A bounded linear map commutes with those sums and limits. Applying this to Dinv Y_n' over an interval of length at most tau gives the assertion; the same calculus differentiates C_n, Q_n and F_n in S001-S002.

background_notes.fact: Writing d=f_n-w, trilinearity gives Cop_I(f_n,f_n,f_n)-Cop_I(w,w,w)=Cop_I(d,f_n,f_n)+Cop_I(w,d,f_n)+Cop_I(w,w,d). With I=[t_n,t], the given static estimates imply ||Cop_I(f_n,f_n,f_n)||_2 <= C_gamma M0^3 tau^gamma + C_0 delta_n[(M0+1)^2+M0(M0+1)+M0^2], hence <=C_(M0,gamma) q_n.

background_notes.justification: Insert one slot difference at a time and expand the trilinear expressions. The bounded extensions preserve this identity: approximate their slots by Fourier polynomials and pass through the supplied continuous maps. The gamma estimate bounds the w-only term, while each sigma=0 estimate bounds its difference term by the product of the three L2 norms, one of which is delta_n.
